title: When Azure SQL Becomes an Application Platform- APIs, Automation and AI with Dirceu Resende
description:
Most teams still treat Azure SQL as passive storage behind the application. In this interview, Dirceu Resende shows data engineers and architects how Azure SQL Database can call REST APIs, automate workflows and support AI with vector search. You learn where this simplifies your architecture and how to keep it secure and performant.
In this episode
00:00 – Intro: Azure SQL as an application platform02:55 – Dirceu's path into data and Power BI09:20 – Azure SQL Database vs. Managed Instance16:42 – Beyond traditional data storage27:46 – REST integrations and automation examples41:12 – Security, authentication and error handling48:33 – Performance, AI and vector search57:03 – BI, governance and rapid fire
Key takeaways
Azure SQL Database can call external REST APIs directly, so the database can trigger alerts, enrich data with AI and integrate with services without extra application code.Secure these integrations with firewalls, least privilege, dedicated users, masking and encryption, and store API secrets in database credential objects instead of in procedures.In the cloud, performance tuning directly lowers cost, and Fabric mirroring offers a near real-time path to BI without hand-built ETL pipelines.
Worth quoting
“Also, the database needs a special attention on it, because you can version code, but you cannot version data. So data is pretty critical and pretty important.” – Dirceu Resende (20:20)
“I understand this concern is really real. But if you can hack into the database, you already have access to all the data anyway.” – Dirceu Resende (41:56)
